collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and an elder)

collection.description: A villager proudly sings a new song, and an elder joins in word for word: laugh about it, or say yours is different.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has made up a new song, and is very proud of it. Tonight (subject.he/she) sings it at the fire. It's lovely. Halfway through, (friend) begins to sing along quietly, word for word. It's an old song. (friend) learned it as a child. (subject) must have heard it long ago, forgotten it, and remembered it as (subject.his/her) own.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: When the song ends, (subject) turns to (friend). "You know it?" "Since I was small." (subject) laughs and covers (subject.his/her) face. "I was so proud of it." "You should be," says (friend). "You remembered it better than any of us. I'd lost the second verse years ago."

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: "Mine has a different ending," says (subject). Everyone waits. (subject) sings an ending that (subject.he/she) is making up right there and then. It's actually rather good. (friend) nods slowly. "That part's new," (friend.he/she) admits. From then on, the village sings the old song with (subject)'s ending.
